chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said during the standing (at Arafat): 'Ascend from the bottom of Batin Urnah.' And he said: 'Indeed, the people of Al-Arak have no Hajj.'

The basis of inference from these two reports is that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) invalidated the Hajj of anyone who left the boundary of Arafat, even if he was standing. Had the standing in it not been obligatory, he would not have invalidated the Hajj of one who stood outside its boundary; rather, he would have permitted him to not stand at all. As for what was narrated:

key_terms.أَصْحَابَ الْأَرَكَ: The people of Al-Arak (a specific tribe or group associated with a boundary marker)
key_terms.بَطْنِ عُرَنَةَ: The bottom/valley of Urnah (a specific location/boundary)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on leaving the boundary of Arafat during the standing of Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the juridical consensus that Wuquf at Arafat is a fundamental pillar (rukn) of Hajj, not merely a sunnah. The Prophet’s specific dismissal of the 'people of Al-Arak'—those who stood outside the canonical boundaries—serves as a critical exegetical proof that validity is contingent upon remaining within the prescribed limits, thereby distinguishing a complete Hajj from an incomplete one.
